nw.name: North & West
nw.bounds: North and west of the late-season goose line: I-95 at the Connecticut line north to Exit 3 (Route 138) in Richmond; east on Route 138 to Glen Rock Road; north on Glen Rock Road to Mail Road, Exeter; east on Mail Road to Route 2 (South County Trail); north on Route 2 to Exeter Road; east on Exeter Road to Indian Corner Road and on to where it merges with West Allenton Road; east to Route 4; south on Route 4 to Route 1 (Tower Hill Road); south on Route 1 to Route 138; east on Route 138 to the base of the Jamestown Bridge; north-northeast along the Washington/Newport county line; east, 1,000 feet north of the northern tip of Jamestown, to a point 1,000 feet off the Melville boat launch in Portsmouth; north, 1,000 feet off Portsmouth’s western shore, to the Mount Hope Bridge; then east-northeast across Mount Hope Bay to the Massachusetts line.
nw.note: Rhode Island sets every waterfowl season statewide except one: the late Canada goose season (Jan 30 – Feb 13, 2027) is open only here — Providence, Bristol and Kent counties, northern Washington County and Prudence Island. The two Rhode Island areas on this map exist only for that season.

se.name: South & East
se.bounds: South and east of the late-season goose line: I-95 at the Connecticut line north to Exit 3 (Route 138) in Richmond; east on Route 138 to Glen Rock Road; north on Glen Rock Road to Mail Road, Exeter; east on Mail Road to Route 2 (South County Trail); north on Route 2 to Exeter Road; east on Exeter Road to Indian Corner Road and on to where it merges with West Allenton Road; east to Route 4; south on Route 4 to Route 1 (Tower Hill Road); south on Route 1 to Route 138; east on Route 138 to the base of the Jamestown Bridge; north-northeast along the Washington/Newport county line; east, 1,000 feet north of the northern tip of Jamestown, to a point 1,000 feet off the Melville boat launch in Portsmouth; north, 1,000 feet off Portsmouth’s western shore, to the Mount Hope Bridge; then east-northeast across Mount Hope Bay to the Massachusetts line.
se.note: Closed during the late Canada goose season (Jan 30 – Feb 13, 2027): southern Washington County, Jamestown, Aquidneck Island, Tiverton, Little Compton, Block Island and the coastal waters. Every other season is statewide.

seasons.label: Sea ducks
seasons.note: Rhode Island has no separate sea duck season or area — scoters, eiders and long-tailed ducks follow the duck season, 4 a day inside the 6.

seasons.label: Canada geese — early
seasons.note: Shooting hours run to half an hour after sunset in this season only.

seasons.label: Canada geese — regular
seasons.note: White-fronted geese count in the 2-goose limit. South Shore Management Area: SSMA permit and field reservation required.

seasons.label: Canada geese — late
seasons.note: North & West area only. The South Shore Management Area is closed.

seasons.label: Snow geese
seasons.note: Blue geese count as snow geese. No possession limit.

seasons.label: Mourning dove
seasons.note: Eurasian collared-doves count in the same limit.

seasons.label: Crows
seasons.note: The first and last segments are Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays only. Patience Island is closed to crow hunting.

bags.detail: Six ducks a day in the aggregate, inside which the species limits below apply. Mergansers are in addition to the six; coots have their own limit.
Common, red-breasted and hooded — in addition to the 6-duck bag.
Scoters, eiders and long-tailed ducks: 4 a day in total, no more than 3 scoters, 3 eiders (1 hen) or 3 long-tailed ducks — inside the 6-duck bag.
Late season, North & West area only.
Sora and Virginia rails: three, singly (the rule’s wording).
Sora and Virginia rails: three, singly (the rule’s wording).
King and clapper rails: one, singly.
Mourning and Eurasian collared-doves in the aggregate.
No daily or possession limit. No HIP needed for crows.

duckSublimits.note: 2 a day from January 5 to 24, 2027 (and on youth and veteran days)
scoters, eiders, long-tailed ducks — no more than 3 of each, eiders no more than 1 hen
any species — in addition to the 6-duck bag
closed — they winter off Sachuest Point and Beavertail; hens look like bufflehead, goldeneye or scoter hens

rules.d: Rhode Island has no Sunday closure for migratory birds. Town ordinances and individual management areas can still restrict hunting.
One-half hour before sunrise to sunset. September Canada geese and crows: one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset.
No loaded firearm outside legal shooting hours, except that a stationary hunter may load within 15 minutes before they begin.
Required for waterfowl, rails and snipe statewide, including tidal waters out to three miles. Nothing larger than BB (duplex loads included), and no tin shot.
No larger than 10 gauge, plugged with a one-piece filler to hold no more than three shells. No rifles, pistols or crossbows; archery requires a bowhunter education course.
No recorded or electronically amplified calls. No live decoys. No hunting over bait — an area stays baited for 10 days after the bait is gone, whether or not you knew it was there.

No shooting from a motorboat or sailboat unless the motor is off or the sail furled and it has stopped moving. No driving or rallying birds with a motorboat, sailboat or vehicle. Sink boxes are illegal.
No firearm discharge within 500 feet of an occupied dwelling without written permission.

200 square inches on state management areas, undeveloped state parks and co-op units from the second Saturday in September to the end of February (500 during shotgun deer season). Waterfowl hunters in a boat or blind with decoys are exempt.

New for 2026–27: no shooting a bird without a visible way to retrieve it. Make a reasonable effort to retrieve every bird, and count it in your bag. In Little Compton and at Great Swamp you must carry a way to retrieve — a retrieving dog or a non-motorized boat.

During the regular Canada goose season, goose hunting at the SSMA (South Kingstown) needs an SSMA permit and a field reservation. Closed during the late goose season. Other waterfowl after the crops are in, without a permit, outside the regular goose season.

Seekonk River above the railroad bridge; Brush Neck, Mill and Buttonwoods coves (Warwick); Mill Cove and western Fishing Cove (Wickford); Watchaug Pond and Poquiant Brook plus 100 yards; the Emilie Ruecker estuary (Tiverton); the Sachuest Point refuge shoreline; Valley Marshes (Lincoln/Central Falls); most of the Barrington River; Belleville Pond except its signed northwest part (after November 15). The red areas on this map are RIDEM’s.

Seekonk River, Barrington River, Walker Island (Bristol), East Providence, Rock Island (Warwick), and Pawtuxet Cove north to Fields Point (Cranston, no shooting within 500 feet of occupied buildings): discharge only toward open water.
October 24–25. Ages 12–17 with a licensed adult 21 or older, who may not hunt. Ducks, mergansers, coots, geese and brant at regular limits; scaup 2.
November 10–11. Proof of eligibility on you, plus HIP, the state waterfowl stamp and the federal duck stamp. Regular limits; scaup 2.

Leave the head or one fully feathered wing on every bird (doves excepted) until you get it home. Tag any birds you leave with someone else: your signature, address, the number by species and the dates taken.

licences.d: From rio.ri.gov, licence agents or DEM. A first licence needs a hunter education certificate (or a previous licence from any state).
Free; added to your licence through rio.ri.gov, agents or DEM. Not needed for crows.
$9.50 for residents, $10 for non-residents (access fee included). A signed stamp, or the stamp certification added to your licence on rio.ri.gov.
Carry it signed in ink across the face. Post office, USPS.com, or an e-stamp at duckstamp.com.

licences.d: Regular Canada goose season only, with a field reservation. From rio.ri.gov or the Great Swamp field headquarters, West Kingston.
